answer: Every clear night the observer estimates a variable star's brightness and files the figure, drawing its curve over months. A velvet estimate guessed indoors fails the ledger: at the willow of the curve the brightness must rise and fall as the star actually does, and a guessed curve is smooth where the star is ragged. To fake the ledger a forger must estimate for 300 nights, draw 20 curves and pay 9,900, and the terrace figure is checked against the comparison stars nightly, so an estimate made under a roof is thrown out.
